links.outcome: Frequency of critical errors (hallucinations, omissions) in LLM output by prompt task type
links.effect: Open-ended conclusion generation from findings produced the highest frequency of critical errors, such as clinically relevant hallucinations or omissions; source text-anchored tasks received the highest utility ratings.
links.quote: Source text-anchored tasks, such as report corrections or simplifications, and radiology guideline recommendations received the highest utility ratings, whereas open-ended conclusion generation based on findings resulted in the highest frequency of critical errors, such as clinically relevant hallucinations or omissions.

unlisted_practices: Isolation-first on-premise LLM architecture with network segmentation, egress filtering, and isolation monitoring
Self-hosting open-weights LLMs for processing unanonymized PHI
Institutional governance approval pathway (management, compliance, data protection, security officers)

screen.reason: The paper implements and prospectively evaluates an on-premise, secure deployment architecture (network isolation, egress filtering, active monitoring) for LLM usage by clinicians in daily radiology workflow.

primary.practice: isolation-first network segmentation and egress filtering
